analysis: photon-level equivalence of the replay kernel against the production kernel
verdict: pass, the gate can fail and the real replay is accepted; the pMC route is unblocked
production_physics_unmodified: nothing under the production tree was edited; the replay module imports the Fresnel reflectance, the Henyey-Greenstein sampler, the direction update and the termination constants from it rather than copying them
other_projects_replay_kernels_not_used_a: P5's replay kernel was instrumented against a different production kernel. The method was borrowed; the implementation was written against this kernel and verified here.
backend_note: bitwise agreement under one XLA backend does not carry over to another, so a pilot must run against a gate taken on its own backend

negative_control.purpose: confirm the gate can fail; a replay whose random-number stream differs must be rejected by the same criteria that accept the real one
negative_control.defect_injected: the outer loop swaps the two halves of the free-path key split, so the key carried forward and the key used for tau are exchanged. The physics is untouched; only the random-number consumption order changes.

a_rejected_candidate_control.candidate: split the key three ways and discard one output
a_rejected_candidate_control.why_it_was_rejected: JAX's threefry split is a prefix, so split(k, 3)[:2] is bitwise equal to split(k, 2) and the stream is unchanged. The gate correctly reported zero mismatches for it, which is why it is not a usable control.

trajectory_invariants_held_fixed: same layer boundaries and optical properties
consequence_for_the_pilot: the pMC route is unblocked and the pilot may include it
